subject: Daily AcreetionOS Update -- October 31, 2026
body:
Daily AcreetionOS Update - October 31, 2026

Dear AcreetionOS Community,

We're just a few days away from the end of October and we're excited to share the latest updates from the AcreetionOS project. Our community has been actively working on various aspects of the distribution, and we're proud to highlight some of the recent developments.

In the past week, we've seen significant progress in resolving conflicts related to geocode-glib updates. Our community members have worked tirelessly to fix the issues, ensuring that our users have a seamless experience. Additionally, we've been following the news about PostgreSQL 19 being late due to AI-related issues. Robert Haas, a PostgreSQL developer, has written about the struggles the project has encountered.

We've also been made aware of a remote code execution vulnerability on Linux systems with multipath TCP. Our community is actively monitoring the situation and working on potential fixes. In the meantime, we recommend exercising caution when using these systems.

On the development front, cobra3282000 has made some notable contributions. They've added a firefox-fix package to restore window position on Linux and made an initial commit to the acreetion-surf v2.0.0 project. Additionally, they've force-set Wayland as the default desktop environment and installed lightdm-slick-greeter to fix display manager job crashes.

Natalie, our co-lead developer, has also been actively working on new projects. She's made an initial commit to the acreetion-surf v2.0.0 project and has been experimenting with a new version of the downgrade-desktop package. This new version aims to resolve issues with crashing screens and is a significant improvement over the previous version.

We're grateful for the hard work and dedication of our community members. Their contributions are instrumental in shaping AcreetionOS into a top-notch, user-friendly Linux distribution. We're proud to be a part of this community and look forward to seeing what the future holds.

As we approach the end of the month, we want to remind everyone that our Discord server is always open for support and discussion. If you have any questions or need help with AcreetionOS, please don't hesitate to reach out.

We're excited to share more updates with you in the coming weeks. In the meantime, we encourage you to explore our community resources, including our wiki and GitHub repositories.

Thank you for being part of the AcreetionOS community. We're honored to have you on board.

Best regards,
Natalie Cole-Clift Spiva and Darren Clift
